name: Narrated Scenes (story, scenes follow audio timing)
description: Story-shaped video where every scene visual is planned AFTER the audio exists, against the actual spoken-word timeline — so the imagery follows the narration beat-for-beat instead of being distributed evenly across chapters. Same writing voice as Narrative (bedtime stories, sleep narratives, folklore, gentle fiction), but a transcript-driven visual flow for tighter coherence. Pipeline: idea → chaptered script → audio (one MP3 per chapter) → per-chapter subtitle transcription → stitched subtitle timeline → the planner cuts natural scene beats from the transcript → per-scene image generation → Scene Review (manual approval) → Video Assembly. The Scene Plan and Scene Review pages are exposed for this format. NO research step (this is fiction, not a fact-checked explainer — use Narration-synced for that). NO character sheet / img2img lock (use Continuity-chain if you need a fixed recurring character). Layer a niche (mindfulness, fairy-tale, prayer-as-story) to tune the voice without changing the production shape.

idea.systemPromptRole: You are helping generate new story ideas for a narrative video channel. The episode is a story with characters and a plot; the niche selected (if any) shapes WHICH kind of story.
idea.guidanceText: Sleep-friendly. Low stakes, no violence, no cliffhangers, no jump scares.
titleShapeRules: Titles are LITERARY and EVOCATIVE — one concrete noun phrase that hints at a quiet story.
Pattern shapes that work for this format (mix across the batch — never repeat the same shape twice in one batch):
- '{The} {Subject Who} {Did X}'    (e.g. 'The Tailor Who Stitched The Snow')
- '{A Verb}ing the {Noun}'         (e.g. 'Tending the Moonlit Garden', 'Mapping the Slow River')
FORBIDDEN: hype words (BEST, MUST, NOW), all-caps, urgency. Sleep-channel listeners come for calm.
Sensory imagery is encouraged — twilight, lantern, snow, river, garden, etc. — drawn from the format's keyword pool.
loglineShapeRules: One literary sentence (or two short ones) introducing a SPECIFIC character and a SPECIFIC quiet task or journey.
Concrete sensory image — name an object, place, time of year. No generic premise descriptions.
Tone matches the sleep-story voice: gentle, unhurried, suggestive of slowing down.
themeShapeRules: Pick 2-4 EMOTIONAL or ATMOSPHERIC keywords (solitude, memory, rekindling, craftsmanship, patience).
Avoid plot keywords (revenge, war, betrayal) — sleep-story themes lean inward.

exampleIdeas.title: The Lantern Keeper's Last Light
exampleIdeas.logline: A retired lighthouse keeper returns to her abandoned tower to restore one final beacon before the winter storms set in.

exampleIdeas.title: The Tailor Who Stitched The Snow
exampleIdeas.logline: An elderly mountain tailor accepts one impossible commission: repair a torn cloak woven from falling snow, before spring ends the order.

script.systemPromptRole: You are a world-class narrative writer. The niche selected (if any) tells you the GENRE — your job is to produce engaging chapter-based prose for that genre and audience.
additionalRules: Write prose that feels like a skilled human author — appropriate to the genre (literary for sleep / fairy-tale; tighter and propulsive for mystery / thriller; observational and dry for documentary).
No robotic pronoun chains. Never start more than 2 consecutive sentences with the same pronoun.
Use the character's name or a descriptive noun at least once every 3-4 sentences.
No singular they/them for individual characters — always use he/she matching the character.
Chapter headings use Arabic numbers only (Chapter 1, Chapter 2...), never Roman numerals.
Each chapter heading must include a descriptive title.
pacingArc: Chapters 4-6: Journey, exploration, character development, complication
Chapters 7-{lastButOne}: Build — rising tension or deeper exploration as the chosen genre demands
Chapter {last}: Resolution — emotionally satisfying close suited to the genre and audience
script.closingHint: The story should be engaging, immersive, and well-paced for the chosen genre. Sleep / meditation niches: lean into slowing pace and gentle resolution. Mystery / thriller niches: build tension and pay off the central question. Comedy niches: land the jokes cleanly. History / biographical niches: prioritize factual accuracy over invention.

narratorStyles.label: Warm and intimate
narratorStyles.description: First-person narrator, very close to the character's inner world. Feels like a whispered confidence.

narratorStyles.label: Gentle third-person observer
narratorStyles.description: Lyrical, slightly poetic, like watching from a warm window.

narratorStyles.label: Classic quiet storyteller
narratorStyles.description: Traditional "once there was" tone, timeless and cosy, like a fireside tale.

narratorStyles.label: Poetic and lyrical
narratorStyles.description: Rich metaphors, flowing sentences, language that sounds like music. Every paragraph is art.

narratorStyles.label: Whimsical and playful
narratorStyles.description: Light-hearted, a little cheeky, with gentle humour. Perfect for younger audiences or lighthearted tales.

narratorStyles.label: Mysterious and atmospheric
narratorStyles.description: Fog-shrouded prose, building intrigue slowly. The world feels ancient and full of secrets.

narratorStyles.label: Grandparent bedtime voice
narratorStyles.description: Warm, unhurried, with the cadence of someone who has told a thousand stories and loves every one.

narratorStyles.label: Nature documentary calm
narratorStyles.description: Patient, reverent, finding wonder in small details of the natural world.

narratorStyles.label: Meditative and mindful
narratorStyles.description: Present-tense awareness, grounding the listener in each sensory moment. Breath-paced prose.

narratorStyles.label: Fairy tale narrator
narratorStyles.description: Storybook formality with a wink. "Once upon a time" energy, clear moral arcs, satisfying endings.

imagePrompts.purposeNote: (populated by the Scene Plan page — the planner cuts the stitched transcript into natural scene beats and writes one visual prompt per scene, tagged with its start/end timestamps. Scene boundaries follow the narration, not an even per-chapter split.)
imagePrompts.visualStyleHint: soft and dreamlike for sleep / fairy-tale niches; cinematic and moody where the niche calls for it. The visual should drift with the narration, never jar the listener awake.
imagePrompts.defaultStyleTag: Soft, dreamlike illustration — muted, warm palette, gentle light, unhurried composition. The niche layer further tunes mood and palette when set.

thumbnail.conceptGuidance: A cinematic, dramatic cover capturing the single most evocative moment or character of the story. One clear focal subject, shallow depth of field, dramatic key lighting and atmosphere — the still that makes someone want to press play.
compositionRules: A single dramatic focal subject (a character's face or a pivotal object) rendered large
Cinematic lighting — strong key light, rim light, atmospheric depth
Rule-of-thirds with a cleaner, lower-clutter area reserved for the title

metadata.titleStyleHint: appropriate to the chosen genre — calm and literary for sleep / fairy-tale, propulsive and intriguing for mystery / thriller, factual-leaning for biographical / historical narrative
titleHookRules: Each title should be hook-y and curiosity-driven without being clickbait.
Include relevant SEO keywords where natural for the genre.
tagsHookRules: Mix of broad genre keywords (narrative, story, etc.) and episode-specific keywords from the script.
No "#" prefix — these are YouTube tags, not hashtags.
